attack_surfaces.operation: mmap RWX + read + call rax (shellcode execution)
attack_surfaces.reason: User-controlled data is read into an RWX mmap region at fixed address 0x13370000 and then executed via call rax. The is_all_upper filter restricts bytes to {0x20, 0x30-0x39, 0x41-0x5a} (space, digits, uppercase letters) but this is a constrained shellcode challenge, not a blocked one. S2 should analyze which syscalls/instructions are achievable with the allowed byte set.

attack_surfaces.operation: byte filter using ctype_b_loc (isupper 0x100 OR isdigit 0x800 OR space 0x20)
attack_surfaces.reason: The filter name suggests uppercase-only but actually allows digits (0x800=_ISdigit not _ISalpha). S2 should verify the exact allowed byte set and whether it enables meaningful shellcode construction.

attack_surfaces.operation: register values leaked via printf before call rax
attack_surfaces.reason: Register state (rax,rbx,rcx,rdx,rbp,rsp,rsi,rdi,r8-r13) is printed to stdout before shellcode execution, providing runtime addresses (stack, libc data pointers) to the shellcode. This is an information leak by design.

facts.description: Binary is statically linked ELF64 x86-64, not stripped, No PIE (base 0x400000)
Security: Partial RELRO, NX enabled, Canary enabled, No PIE, CET (IBT+SHSTK) enabled
No dynamic section, no NEEDED libraries, no RPATH/RUNPATH - fully static link
main (0x4018dd) calls mmap(0x13370000, 0x64, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE|PROT_EXEC, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) creating a 100-byte RWX region at fixed hint 0x13370000
main calls memset(mmap_buf, 0, 100) then read(0, mmap_buf, 99) to read shellcode from stdin
If last byte of read input is 0x0a (newline), it is replaced with 0x00 (NUL)
is_all_upper (0x401819) filters shellcode bytes: each byte must satisfy isupper (ctype 0x100) OR isdigit (ctype 0x800) OR equal 0x20 (space). Allowed bytes: {0x20, 0x30-0x39, 0x41-0x5a}
If is_all_upper returns 0, _abort prints 'invalid shellcode!' and exits(1)
After filter passes, main prints all register values (rax-r13) then restores them and executes call rax (0x401b4b) jumping to shellcode at 0x13370000
init (0x4017aa) sets stdin/stdout/stderr to unbuffered (setvbuf _IONBF) and calls alarm(60)
Runtime confirmed: input 'AAAA' (all uppercase) passes filter and executes (SIGSEGV on invalid instructions). Input 'aaaa' (lowercase) is rejected. Input '1234' (digits) passes filter and executes.
Register state leaked at runtime includes stack address (rsp/rbp) and libc data segment addresses (rbx points near 0x7fff...), providing ASLR bypass info to shellcode
No seccomp/prctl/sandbox calls found in binary - shellcode has full syscall access
Shellcode max size is 99 bytes (read size = mmap_size - 1 = 0x64 - 1 = 99)

Allowed shellcode byte set is 37 values: {0x20, 0x30-0x39, 0x41-0x5a}. This includes x86 instructions like PUSH imm (0x68 not allowed), but 0x41-0x4f are REX prefixes, 0x50-0x5a are PUSH reg, 0x30-0x39 include XOR/CMP opcodes. S2 should analyze constructable shellcode.

uncertainties.description: Whether mmap returns exactly 0x13370000 or a different address at runtime
uncertainties.reason: mmap hint is 0x13370000 but kernel may return different address; runtime probe showed rax=0x13370000 printed, suggesting hint is honored, but ASLR status unknown

uncertainties.description: Whether CET (IBT/SHSTK) actually restricts shellcode execution at runtime
uncertainties.reason: IBT requires endbr64 at indirect call targets; the mmap region is filled with user data without endbr64 prefix.
